answer: An agent economy can make voting power depend on a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation score: each agent starts at the nadir, gains weight only after peers validate useful work across separate tasks, and loses weight when audits expose fabricated claims. A kernel of randomly selected reviewers checks evidence before credit is granted, while a summit threshold limits any one identity’s influence. A sybil attacker must therefore sustain many agents through costly, verifiable contributions, rather than minting names cheaply; collusion risks audits and wasted effort.
